claims.claim: Photius was Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 858 to 867 and from 877 to 886.
Photius was born c. 815 and died 6 February 893.
Photius is recognized in the Eastern Orthodox Church as 'Saint Photius the Great'.
The Fragmenta in epistulam ad Hebraeos survives as fragments in catenas (chain commentaries).
The Fragmenta in epistulam ad Hebraeos is published in Migne's Patrologia Graeca, volume 101, columns 1253-1254.
Photius was a leading figure of the 9th-century Byzantine renascence and one of the most famous scholars of the Middle Ages.
Before becoming patriarch, Photius was professor of philosophy at the University of Constantinople.
Photius was appointed patriarch in 858 while still a layman, being ordained and quickly elevated to the office.
Manuscripts of Photius's Pauline commentaries survive in collections including Oxford, Magdalen College, gr. 007.
